text:
alex: Heads up — CI perf jobs show a regression on Mixtral-8x at ~512 seq after the kernel-selection change yesterday. Numbers below, cc @maria @jamie.

alex: Perf run summary (60s gen, 1 token steps):
```
model: mixtral-8x
old-kernel: 23.1 ms/token
new-kernel: 35.7 ms/token  # +55% at 512
seq=64: old 6.2ms, new 6.8ms
seq=256: old 15.0ms, new 20.4ms
seq=512: huge gap pulls avg up
```

alex: Logs show a fallback to the generic attention path at hot loops: `kernel_selector: fallback=generic_attn`. Not sure why it didn't pick the optimized matmul+kv path.

maria: Oof. I noticed Mixtral's HF config is missing explicit `rope_scaling` fields in the converted config we ship. Could be RoPE scaling mismatch causing weird kernel triggers.

jamie: Can you paste the model config snippet from the repo? I remember we have a conversion script that tries to infer head/kvdims, but it was brittle for 8x variants.

alex: Pasted from `models/mixtral-8x/config.json` on staging: `"n_head": 32, "n_key_value_heads": null, "kv_dim": 64, "rotary_pct": 0.25` — note `n_key_value_heads` is null (weird). Conversion script set `n_key_value_heads` to null when not in hf_meta.

sanya: That null could be tripping kernel selector which expects `n_kv_heads` int to decide packed KV kernel. If it gets null => fall back.

perf-bot: regression alert: mixtral-8x@staging CPU/GPU avg token latency +55% vs baseline (2026-03-16). Link: https://perf.internal/runs/1762003400

jamie: Quick repro attempt locally. I replaced null with 8 in config and re-ran. Result: new-kernel selected optimized path and latency dropped back to ~24 ms/token at 512. So it's a config-parsing bug.

alex: Nice. Do we know why HF conversion left it null? Usually HF uses `n_kv_heads` or `n_key_value_heads` keys — different models use different names. Our parser looked only for `n_kv_heads`.

maria: Also found a subtle RoPE scaling mismatch for Mixtral vs Mistral derivatives: our runtime applies scaling when `rope_scaling: { "factor": x }` exists; if absent, we assume 1.0. But Mixtral expects alpha-based scaling (scale by sqrt(alpha) in some conversions). That can change the attention temperature and push kernel heuristics (precision choices).

jamie: Actionable items: 1) patch HF conversion to canonicalize `n_key_value_heads` (fill from `n_kv_heads` or compute n_head // 4 heuristic), 2) add a unit test that ensures kernel selector sees an int, 3) add RoPE canonicalization step to conversion script.

sanya: I'll open a quick PR with a safe fallback: if `n_key_value_heads` is null, compute `n_key_value_heads = max(1, n_head // (n_kv_head_divisor || 4))` and persist it. Also add a warning log so we can trace future fallbacks.

alex: For immediate mitigation on prod: can we add a kernel-selector override that forces optimized KV path for known Mixtral variants? Temporary env var `RUNTIME_FORCE_KV_KERNELS=mixtral-*`.

maria: I'd rather fix configs; but okay for emergency. Also want to record an eval check: ensure token-level perplexity doesn't shift when we canonicalize RoPE scaling. Differences could indicate subtle semantic regressions.

jamie: I'll add a quick perf CI job that runs mixtral/mistral/qwen permutations (rope scaling toggled) at seq=64/256/512 and fails on >15% token latency regression.

ci-bot: Job created: `perf/eng-runtime/mixtral-kv-config-check #287` triggered by jamie — results will post when done.

sanya: I'll land the conversion patch and a small script to patch existing model bundles with missing kv heads. Script:```bash
# fill_kv_heads.sh
python -c "import json,sys
p=sys.argv[1]
c=json.load(open(p))
if c.get('n_key_value_heads') in (None,'null'):
  c['n_key_value_heads']=max(1, c['n_head']//4)
  json.dump(c, open(p,'w'), indent=2)
  print('patched',p)
else:
  print('ok',p)
" models/mixtral-8x/config.json
```

alex: Great. Let's prioritize: (1) CI perf job (jamie) (2) conversion + patch (sanya) (3) RoPE canonicalization + eval checks (maria). I'll own the rollback override for prod if we see traffic impact.

maria: Thanks. Can we also add a small runtime metric: `kernel_selector.decision` tag on traces so we know which path was taken for each request? That'll help postmortems.

alex: Yup I'll add it to the tracer.

jamie: Noted. I'll follow up with the job link and initial CI numbers. :thumbsup:

sanya: PR coming in ~1h.

alex: Closing loop — please drop results here and ping me if anything blocks the rollout.
